raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year's plan.

---

*I'm 75 now, been working this land since I was a boy. My wife helps when she can, but the two sons work in town — they send money but can't come back for busy seasons. So it's mostly me and hired help for the heavy days.*

*Six mu isn't much. I keep one mu for cotton because I've always done it and I know that land — it's the strip that doesn't flood-irrigate well, so cotton suits it. The other five mu I do wheat and maize, same as everyone around here. That's the way we do it in Quzhou.*

*For the wheat, I plant after the Double Ninth festival, around mid-October. I use my own saved seed — my neighbor says the new varieties yield better but the seed costs money and I'm not sure. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu — that's about 50 kg. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green and starts jointing, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. I water before winter, once at jointing, and once more when it's heading if the sky is dry. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, that's about what I expect.*

*Right after wheat harvest in early June, there's no time to waste. I clear the straw, hire the little rotary tiller from Old Wang next door for 30 yuan per mu, and plant maize within three or four days. I use hybrid seed — can't save maize seed, everyone buys fresh. At planting I put some urea in the row, and then when the maize is at big trumpet stage (about knee-high) I topdress more urea. If July is dry I'll irrigate once, but usually the rain comes. Maize I get around 450 kg per mu most years.*

*Cotton is more trouble than it's worth for an old man, but I've grown it all my life. Plant after grain rain, mid-April, under film. I put one bag of compound before planting and a little urea when it starts squaring. The bollworms and aphids — I spray two or three times, that's where cotton eats up money. Picking is slow, I do it by hand over several weeks. My wife helps with picking. I won't get more than 220 kg of lint per mu, but the price is usually decent.*

*I don't spend money I don't have. If something looks bad I'll add a little fertilizer, but I don't chase big yields. Better to keep some cash for the grandkids.*
